items.title: 9.13 Resistivity aur temperature par us ka inhisar (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 9.13 with Fig. 9.22, Table 9.2 and Examples 9.7 and 9.8 (PDF 210-212).

blocks.text: Tajurbe se dekha gaya hai ke taar ki resistance R us ki lambai L ke seedhe tanasub mein aur us ke cross-sectional area A ke ulte tanasub mein hoti hai. Formula mein:

Yahan ρ (rho) proportionality constant hai jise taar ke material ki resistivity ya specific resistance kehte hain. Yaad rakhein: resistance ek khaas taar ki khasiyat hai (lambai aur motai par munhasir), jabke resistivity us material ki khasiyat hai jis se taar bana hai. Eq. 9.32 se:
Is se resistivity ki tareef milti hai: kisi material ke ek metre cube (1 m lamba, 1 m² area) ki resistance. Resistivity ki SI unit ohm-metre (Ω m) hai.
Conductance bhi materials ki electrical khasiyat batane wali quantity hai. Conductance resistance ka ulat (reciprocal) hai:
Isi tarah conductivity σ (sigma) resistivity ρ ka ulat hai:

Conductivity ki SI unit ohm⁻¹ m⁻¹ ya mho m⁻¹ hai. Mukhtalif materials ki resistivity Table 9.2 mein hai. Table se pata chalta hai ke silver (chandi) aur copper sab se achhe conductors hain. Isi liye zyada tar bijli ke taar copper ke bante hain (silver mehngi hai).

blocks.title: Dhyan dein
blocks.text: Table 9.2 mein platinum ki α (0.00520) aur ρ wahi likhe hain jo iron (loha) ke hain. Aam reference tables mein platinum ki α taqreeban 0.0039 K⁻¹ di jati hai. Kitab ki Example 9.8 bhi isi table jaisi qeemat (5.18 × 10⁻³ K⁻¹) deti hai, is liye exam mein kitab ki qeemat hi istemal karein, magar yeh baat yaad rakhein. ("Constanton" ka sahi naam Constantan hai.)

Kisi material ki resistivity temperature par bhi munhasir hai. Conductor ki resistance is liye hoti hai ke free electrons lattice ke atoms se takrate hain. Temperature barhne se atoms zyada zor se (zyada amplitude ke saath) hilte hain, aur electrons ke un se takrane ka imkan barh jata hai. Yani atoms bara nishana (target) ban jate hain: un ka collision cross-section temperature ke saath barhta hai. Takraav zyada hote hain, is liye conductor ki resistance barh jati hai.

Tajurbe se pata chalta hai ke dhaat ke conductor ki resistance 0°C ke oopar aur neeche kaafi range mein temperature ke saath taqreeban seedhi lakeer (linear) mein badalti hai (Fig. 9.22). Is range mein har kelvin par resistance mein hone wali nisbati (fractional) tabdeeli ko temperature coefficient of resistance (α) kehte hain:

blocks.alt: Graph: khari axis par resistivity rho (ohm m), pari axis par temperature T (degree C) -200 se 600 tak. Magenta lakeer neeche baen se seedhi oopar jati hai; taqreeban 400 degree C ke baad doosra curve seedhi lakeer se thora oopar mur jata hai.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.22: temperature ke saath copper ki resistivity mein tabdeeli (kitab ki Figure 9.22 ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: 0°C ke aas paas bare hisse mein graph taqreeban seedha hai, is liye α qareeban constant hai. Bohat zyada temperature par asal curve seedhi lakeer se thora hat jata hai.
Yahan R_o aur R_t 0°C aur t°C par resistances hain. Resistivity bhi temperature par munhasir hai, is liye Eq. 9.32 se:

blocks.text_alt: R_t = ρ_t L/A   aur   R_o = ρ_o L/A   (9.36)

blocks.text: Eq. 9.36 ki qeematein Eq. 9.35 mein rakhein (L/A cut jata hai):

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab likhti hai "R_t aur R_o ki qeematein Eq. 9.36 mein rakhein"; asal mein yeh Eq. 9.35 mein rakhi jati hain.

Yahan ρ_o 0°C par aur ρ_t t°C par resistivity hai. Kuch materials ke α bhi Table 9.2 mein hain. Germanium, silicon waghaira aise materials hain jin ki resistance temperature barhne se kam hoti hai; in ke temperature coefficients manfi (negative) hain.

blocks.title: Maloomat ke liye (For Your Information)
blocks.text: Inspectors carbon fibres wale concrete pul (bridge) ki mazbooti aasani se jaanch sakte hain. Carbon fibres bijli guzarte hain. Agar sensors dikhayein ke electrical resistance waqt ke saath barh rahi hai to iska matlab hai ke daraaron (cracks) ki wajah se fibres alag ho rahe hain.

blocks.title: Example 9.7
blocks.problem: Lohe (iron) ke taar ke siron par 1.5 V ki battery jorne se us mein 0.75 A current behta hai. Taar 5.0 m lamba hai aur us ka cross-sectional area 2.5 × 10⁻⁷ m² hai. Lohe ki resistivity nikalein.
steps: Pehle resistance (Eq. 9.31 se): R = V/I = 1.5 V/0.75 A = 2.0 Ω
Phir resistivity: ρ = RA/L = (2.0 Ω × 2.5 × 10⁻⁷ m²)/5.0 m

blocks.title: Example 9.8
blocks.problem: Platinum ke taar ki resistance 0°C par 10 Ω aur 193°C par 20 Ω hai. Platinum ka temperature coefficient of resistance nikalein.
steps: Diya gaya: R_o = 10 Ω, R_t = 20 Ω, t = 193°C (temperature ka farq 193 K: 466 K − 273 K)

blocks.prompt: 4 Ω resistance wale taar ko dohra (double) kar diya jaye to nayi resistance kya hogi (MCQ 9.7)? Resistance R wale copper ke taar ko khench kar dugni lambai ka kar diya jaye to nayi resistance kya hogi (short question 9.5)? Temperature barhne par conductor ki resistance kyun barhti hai (short question 9.6)?
blocks.explanation: Dohra karne se L aadhi aur A dugna ho jata hai, is liye R = ρL/A chauthai reh jati hai: 1 Ω, option (d). Dugni lambai tak khenchne se volume wahi rehta hai, is liye area aadha ho jata hai; L/A chaar guna hota hai aur nayi resistance 4R hai. Garam dhaat mein lattice ke atoms zyada zor se hilte hain, free electrons un se zyada baar takrate hain aur un ka drift zyada rukta hai, is liye resistance barhti hai.

items: R = ρL/A (9.32); resistivity ρ = RA/L (9.33), unit Ω m, material ki khasiyat.
Conductance G = 1/R; conductivity σ = 1/ρ (9.34), unit mho m⁻¹. Silver aur copper sab se achhe conductors.
Garam lattice → zyada takraav → zyada R; α = (R_t − R_o)/(R_o t) (9.35) = (ρ_t − ρ_o)/(ρ_o t) (9.37); carbon, germanium, silicon ka α manfi.
Examples: ρ(iron) = 1.0 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m; α(platinum) = 5.18 × 10⁻³ K⁻¹.
